newsitem.title: USA: TRO Q1 loss widens on lower aviation revs.
newsitem.headline: TRO Q1 loss widens on lower aviation revs.

text.p: TRO Learning Inc on Thursday said a decline in revenues from its aviation training courseware in the fiscal first quarter was largely responsible for the company showing a bigger loss than it did a year earlier.
Revenues generated by the courseware were about $1.0 million less than in the first quarter ended January 31, 1996, leading to a decline of $850,000 in gross profit.
In the year-earlier first quarter, TRO received an aviation training order worth more than $1 million.
The company develops a range of microcomputer-based instructional and testing systems.

Revenues from TRO's PLATO Learning Systems courseware showed little change from the 1996 quarter, as did gross profit from PLATO revenue. PLATO programs are marketed to middle and high schools and community colleges, among others.
"The loss for the first quarter was in the range of expectations," Chairman William Roach said in a statement.
Roach said TRO had made progress in marketing PLATO over the Internet in Version 2.0, released in February.
For the quarter ended January 31, TRO said its loss widened to $0.37 per share from $0.17 in the year-earlier period. Total revenues fell to $5.1 million from $6.4 million.
